title: Retail Installment Contracts Training Q&A: The Late-Charge Estimate on a Payoff Statement
content:
*When does a payoff statement on Retail Installment Contracts carry a late-charge estimate?*

When the installment due on the next due date is past due on the quote date but its late-charge grace period has not ended — that is, the quote date is 1 to **10** days (the product's late-charge grace period) after the next due date. Otherwise no estimate is added.

*How much is it?*

- For an installment that is not the final installment: **5.0** percent (the product's late-charge percent) of the scheduled installment, never more than **25.00** (the product's late-charge cap).
- For the final installment, due on the final installment date (maturity date): 5.0 percent of the lesser of the scheduled installment and the principal balance, never more than 25.00.

| Days from the next due date to the quote date | Installment | Estimate |
|---|---|---|
| 0 or fewer (not past due) | any | none |
| 1 to 10 | not the final one | 5.0% of the scheduled installment, at most 25.00 |
| 1 to 10 | the final one | 5.0% of the lesser of the scheduled installment and the principal balance, at most 25.00 |
| 11 or more | any | none |

*Worked figures (hypothetical contracts).*

- Scheduled installment 412.60, quoted 6 days after the next due date: 5.0% of 412.60 is 20.63.
- Scheduled installment 588.00: 5.0% is 29.40, above the cap, so 25.00.
- Final installment, scheduled 412.60, principal balance 233.40: the lesser is 233.40; 5.0% of it is 11.67.
- Quoted 12 days after the next due date: the grace period has ended, so no estimate.
